Margins and sidenotes

By Ines Varga

The committee met in the old library on the hill, where the winter light fell across the long oak tables, and the members argued, as they always did, about the cost of repairing the roof.

Nobody could remember who had first proposed the plan, but by the second hour it had acquired the weight of tradition, and dissent, when it came, was polite and brief.

In the end the treasurer produced a ledger, worn at the corners, and read out the figures in a flat voice that silenced the room, because the numbers, as ever, were worse than anyone had guessed.

Outside, the river rose slowly against the stone bridge, carrying branches and the first ice of the year, and a boy on the far bank counted the pieces as they passed under the arch.
